Subject: CardioAI — ask: 28% hosted-API unit rate concession for Q3 ramp

Marcus / Mina —

Quick background: CardioAI is a clinical workflow customer we’ve been trialing for the last 6 weeks. They’re forecasting a fast ramp to ~12B tokens/mo by month 4 (mainly inference calls for triage models). They’re asking for an upfront unit-rate reduction from our published hosted API list to secure an 18‑month onboarding and a multi‑region deployment (us-east + us-west).

What they’re asking: 28% off list unit rates for hosted text generation tokens (applies to both chat and non-chat endpoints) for months 1–12, with a step-up to 18% for months 13–18. They’ve tied the request to a committed minimum monthly spend ramp schedule (we have the projection attached).

Why it matters:
- High strategic value: will be referenceable in cardiology vertical and could unlock marketplace placement via their cloud partner.
- Volume economics: if forecast holds, this becomes a large predictable revenue stream and justifies an initial concession to accelerate adoption.
- Risk: our unit economics are tight in month 1 given expected QPS patterns and KV cache inefficiency until warm-up; finance needs to verify.

Ask: Marcus — I need exec sign-off for anything >20% to move the concession to legal/procurement. If you’re not available, Mina can approve conditionally with finance constraints.

Attachments: CardioAI_Month1_usage_projection.xlsx (detailed forecast), Draft_SOW_CardioAI.pdf

Proposed next step: quick approval or counteroffer by Friday 12 July so we can lock the cadence into the SOW.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: CardioAI — ask: 28% hosted-API unit rate concession for Q3 ramp

Ben —

Thanks for the summary. I’ll need a short finance check — Jonas, can you validate the blended unit cost and incremental margin at the proposed 28% off list for months 1–12 versus an 18‑month term? Please include GPU-hour amortization for initial warm-up (we should be conservative on cache benefits).

Mina — flagging because this is >20% and strategic. If finance can show positive contribution by month 6 and no material cash drain, I’m inclined to approve a time-limited concession with the following guardrails:
- 12-month guaranteed minimum value (as a fallback)
- Quarterly review and quality SLO tied to token-per-success metric in SOW
- Automatic reversion to standard rates if usage <50% of forecast for two consecutive months

If you’re comfortable with that conditional structure, I can provide an exec approval email to finish legal/procurement loop.

Marcus

Subject: Re: CardioAI — ask: 28% hosted-API unit rate concession for Q3 ramp

Marcus / team —

I ran a quick model (Cost_Model_Redwood_v2.xlsx attached). Short summary:
- At 28% off list, the per-token gross margin falls to ~19% in months 1–3 assuming current kernel mix and cold cache.
- By month 6, with the forecasted cache hit improvements and usage smoothing, margin recovers to ~33%.
- If we include a 12‑month minimum commitment spelled into the SOW (their current proposal is a 18‑month ramp with minimums month-to-month), downside is controlled: 12-month minimum salvages ~+10% margin versus a pure on-demand scenario.

Recommendation: Operationally acceptable provided we: 1) include a firm 12-month minimum committed spend (we should ask Legal to write clawback language), and 2) apply a staged pricing schedule: 28% off months 1–6, 22% off months 7–12, then 12% off months 13–18. That keeps us above a threshold margin during the early ramp while still honoring their ask in part.

If you want a more conservative path: approve 24% for months 1–6, then step to 18% months 7–12. That gives us more runway on cash.

Jonas

Attachment: Cost_Model_Redwood_v2.xlsx
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: CardioAI — ask: 28% hosted-API unit rate concession for Q3 ramp

Team —

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the quick model. I agree with the staged pricing approach as the right balance between competitiveness and protecting unit economics. The deal is strategic for the cardiology vertical and their cloud partner channel is important.

I’m comfortable with the following concession pattern as an exec-level authorization to move to legal/procurement: 1) 26% off list months 1–4, 2) 20% off months 5–12, 3) 12% off months 13–18. Conditions: 12‑month minimum value committed in SOW, monthly usage reporting, and a quarterly business review cadence. Legal should include clawback language if usage diverges >40% negative from forecast for two consecutive months.

Marcus — you can sign off if you’re aligned. Ben — if Marcus signs, proceed with the SOW edits and loop in Legal / Procurement.

Mina
